youtube.title: Saturn Is Less Dense Than Water. Would It Float?
youtube.caption:
Saturn is less dense than water. Would it float? Not quite.

Saturn's average density is lower than water's, so in a thought experiment it floats. Real Saturn is gas and would not stay in one piece.

Series: One More Orbit · Season 2 · Episode 5.

Sources
1. Saturn's mean density (0.687 g/cm3) is below water's (1.0), so on average it is less dense than water. — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/
2. Saturn's equatorial diameter is about 9.4 Earth diameters (120,536 km vs 12,756 km). — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/
3. Saturn is made mostly of hydrogen and helium. — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/
4. Earth's mean density is 5.51 g/cm3, so it sinks in water; Earth is rock and metal. — nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/saturnfact.html
5. Saturn is about 9.5 AU from the Sun; sunlight takes about 80 minutes. — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/
6. Saturn's mean density is 687 kg/m3 (0.687 g/cm3); water is about 1,000 kg/m3, so Saturn weighs less than the same volume of water. — nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/saturnfact.html
7. Saturn is a gas giant with no true surface: mostly swirling gases (and liquids deeper down), so its weight is spread thin. — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/
8. NASA says Saturn 'could float in a bathtub if such a colossal thing existed': a thought experiment, since its average density is below water's. — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/
9. Saturn has no true surface; it is mostly swirling gases and liquids, so real Saturn is not a solid ball that sits on water (it would mix). — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. Sources are listed per claim; each page should be opened by a person before posting.

One More Orbit: One minute, one 'whoa' about the universe, every number sourced.
